upstream.scope: Sampled per-process CPU usage as one defined read-only metric beside PID, name and resident memory, with one logical CPU as 100% and explicit warming-up and unavailable states; no host-normalized display, no sorting, no graphs, no process controls, no macOS source, no htop parity claim

entries.feature: CPU usage is published as a fourth table column headed 'CPU (100% = 1 CPU)': one fully used logical CPU is 100%, so a multithreaded process may exceed it; the value is stored as an exact tick delta, tick rate and monotonic interval and turned into text once on the server in integer arithmetic with the tenths digit truncated
entries.scope: PX-006/fake, scripted and live procfs sources/read-only; a host-normalized percentage is a later display option

entries.feature: A metric definition states the interface the number is read from (/proc/<pid>/stat fields 14 utime and 15 stime in clock ticks, divided by the tick rate the scanned mount reports through AT_CLKTCK and by a monotonic interval) and what it omits (waited-for children's cutime and cstime)
entries.scope: PX-006/metric definition only; the metric registry, scheduling and availability model are PX-042

entries.feature: One persistent collector keeps one counter baseline per published process instance, keyed by PID and creation token: a first sample and a replacement under a reused PID publish 'Warming up'; a counter reset, a zero or backwards monotonic interval, an implausible delta and an unknown tick rate publish 'Unavailable' (or 'Denied'); none of them is ever published as 0.0% or as a spike, a measured zero stays 0.0%, and a different boot or PID namespace discards every baseline
entries.scope: PX-006/live and fixture procfs roots/read-only; baselines bounded by the record bound and forgotten when a process ends

entries.feature: The CPU interval is measured only on an injected monotonic clock, never on the wall clock that stamps the sample, so deterministic counters yield exact single-CPU and multicore percentages independent of wall-clock time
entries.scope: PX-006/collector clock injection; the live clock is Instant (CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux)

entries.feature: On a real Linux kernel a bounded, test-owned, single-threaded busy worker is first published as warming up and then reads within a documented tolerance of one logical CPU, while a test-owned sleeping worker reads near zero, and the measured value reaches the published row through an in-place refresh
entries.scope: PX-006/live procfs source/read-only; tolerances rather than exact scheduler numbers
